solution_sketch: The terms are the first 20 odd numbers (last term 39 = 2·20 − 1). The sum of the first n odd numbers is n², so the total is 20² = 400. You can spot the pattern from 1, 1+3=4, 1+3+5=9, 1+3+5+7=16 — consecutive perfect squares.
difficulty_rationale: Naive route: add 20 numbers head-to-tail in under 20 s — not going to happen. The insight is that 1, 3, 5, … are the odd numbers and their running totals 1, 4, 9, 16 are perfect squares, so the sum of the first n is n². Counting the terms (last term 39 = 2·20 − 1 ⇒ n = 20) gives 20² = 400 in a single mental step. The pattern is reachable cold because the first few partial sums announce themselves, and there is exactly one arithmetic step after the insight.
